title: Rematch: The Quicklime Kid
summary: There's a chalk line across the pan edge of the Drowned Array and your name under it — well, a chalk silhouette of a crate, which is worse. The Quicklime Kid runs the sunken panel-rows at dusk: a slalom through dead glass that punishes speed and rewards nerve. No purse, no purse-strings, no purse-related vocabulary. Just the line.

objectives.label: Meet the chalk line at the pan edge
Run the slalom: panel-rows → drowned substation → back through the rows → the cairn
The return leg — the Kid's own course, reversed through the dust

offer.text: *a chalk line across the pan edge, and beside it, in handwriting that has clearly been practising: YOU RACE SALT NOW. COME RACE GLASS.*

Ash — open band, sorry — if that's the Kid chalking you, GO. That's not a challenge, that's an invitation. Do you know how many riders get the chalk? Three. I've COUNTED. The panel slalom is the best technical course on Kessa-9 and it doesn't technically exist.
Drowned Array's all rhythm, kid. The panel-rows creak a half-second before your line should change — the desert telegraphs down there. Listen to the glass, not your throttle hand.

accept.text: *two short revs, one long one. Then, flat on the band like a weather report:* 'Gates marked. Mine count.' *the visor-grin catches the low sun and is gone into the rows*

Technical notes, since the Kid won't give any: the substation gate is blind — commit BEFORE you see it, the cairn gate comes up fast after, and if a panel creaks under your skirt lift your line, it means the glass remembers weight and is FLATTERING you.
Copy. Blind gate, fast cairn, and the glass is a critic. If I lose to a person with no recorded voice I'm framing the chalk.

complete.text: *the Kid idles beside you, revs twice, pauses — and then, in an actual voice, sanded down from disuse:* 'Good race.' *a glove chalks a tiny finish line across your bow. Terms are terms. The dust settles on it like respect.*

THEY USED A FULL SENTENCE. Ash, do you understand what you hold? I've got riders offering me real credits for transcripts of 'Good race' and I won't sell — principally — because it's YOURS. Frame the chalk, kid. Frame the chalk.
Heard the creak of that slalom from the garage roof — rookies don't make panels sing like that. Flats and a following wind, Varga. You just got adopted by the Array, and the Array's a picky family.
